_README: Australia DFAT Consolidated List (Regulation 8) — maintained in-repo because DFAT bot-gates the .xlsx file (it returns HTTP 404 to automated fetches, serving browsers only), so it cannot be fetched directly. To turn DFAT into a DIRECTLY-screened list: download regulation8_consolidated.xlsx from https://www.dfat.gov.au/international-relations/security/sanctions/consolidated-list, paste each designated party's name into `entries` (a plain string, or {"name":"...","aliases":["..."]} for AKAs), update `count` + `lastReviewed`, then set this source's `enabled:true` in data/sanctions-extra.json. (The dependency-free XLSX reader in scripts/sanctions-match.mjs can parse the file too, if a fetchable URL is ever confirmed.) While `entries` is empty the source stays disabled so it never reports a false clear or a permanent 'degraded' flag. Most DFAT autonomous designations already mirror the UN/OFAC/EU lists screened directly. ACTIVATION: the switch is the 'au-dfat-curated' source in data/sanctions-extra.json (file+curated parser) — flip its enabled:true after populating entries; nothing reads this file until then.
